java_locations.role: Uses one [%pLN_.]+ code grammar for inline and multiline named notes and resolves the complete code through the current quark context.
Defines %pLN as Unicode letters and digits; underscore and dot are the additional code characters supplied by CommandFactoryNote.

rust_locations.role: Uses divergent code tokens: inline captures only a non-anchored word prefix while multiline accepts dots.

claimed_invariant: Inline and multiline Component named notes share the Java code token: one or more Unicode letters, digits, underscores, or dots. The entire legal token becomes ComponentNote.id and participates in known-note lookup, owner qualification, links, UID construction, and SVG identity; no valid suffix may be silently truncated to a word prefix.
causal_divergence: RE_NOTE_INLINE captures only \w+ and is not bounded after the capture, so Ledger.C464 is accepted as Ledger. RE_NOTE_MULTI independently encodes a wider token. The parser therefore changes a valid quark identity before ownership and rendering see it.
planned_model_change: Define one Java-cited note code token and use it in both inline and multiline regexes. Require a command boundary after the inline capture while preserving legal trailing note modifiers for separate parsing. Store and register the complete captured code unchanged.
acceptance: Fresh valid Component-dispatched Java inputs retain the complete named-note code in Rust AST and SVG identity.
Simple ids remain unchanged and invalid punctuation is not accepted as a legal prefix.
Nested dotted ids are qualified once beneath their declaration owner.
An independent checker attacks token boundaries, Unicode, ownership and later references.
forbidden_approaches: special-casing Ledger or any held-out id
splitting dots after parsing or rewriting SVG qualified names
broadening the token to arbitrary punctuation
changing comparator, baseline, park list or error markers
declared_residue: Component connection endpoints still use a narrower grammar and require a separate link-command audit.
Note modifier fields beyond the identity boundary are outside this mechanism.
Multiline terminator spelling is a separate command-body grammar concern.
